parts.speak: Think you know it all? Five questions. No Googling, no lifelines. See how many you can get right, and drop your score in the comments when you are done.
parts.subtitle: 5 questions · No Googling
parts.title: TRIVIA CHALLENGE

parts.display: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
parts.speak: Question one, and this one looks easy. Which planet is known as the Red Planet?

parts.explain: Iron oxide — basically rust — covers its surface.
parts.speak: The answer is Mars. It looks red because of iron oxide, basically rust, covering its surface.

parts.display: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
parts.speak: Question two. What is the largest ocean on Earth?

parts.explain: Bigger than all of Earth's land combined.
parts.speak: The Pacific Ocean. It covers more area than all of Earth's land put together.

parts.display: How many sides does a hexagon have?
parts.speak: Question three. How many sides does a hexagon have?

parts.explain: Six sides, six angles — like a honeycomb cell.
parts.speak: Six. A hexagon has six sides and six angles. Think of a honeycomb cell.

parts.display: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
parts.speak: Question four. What is the chemical symbol for gold?

parts.explain: From aurum, the Latin word for gold.
parts.speak: The letters A and U. The symbol comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

parts.display: In what year did humans first land on the Moon?
parts.speak: Question five, the last one. In what year did humans first land on the Moon?
Nineteen sixty-nine. Apollo Eleven landed on July twentieth, nineteen sixty-nine.
That is your score out of five. Got all five? Then you are officially smarter than the average internet. Follow for round two.

facts.fact: Mars is called the Red Planet because iron oxide (rust) on its surface gives it a reddish appearance.
facts.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
facts.source: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, 'Mars in a Minute: Is Mars Really Red?' — https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/videos/mars-in-a-minute-is-mars-really-red/

facts.fact: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean basin on Earth, covering more than 155 million square kilometers — larger than all of Earth's land combined.
facts.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
facts.source: NOAA Ocean Exploration, 'How big is the Pacific Ocean?' — https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/ocean-fact/pacific-size/

facts.fact: A hexagon is a six-sided polygon with six angles.
facts.question: How many sides does a hexagon have?

facts.fact: Gold's chemical symbol is Au, from the Latin word aurum; gold is element 79.
facts.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
facts.source: Royal Society of Chemistry, Periodic Table, 'Gold' — https://periodic-table.rsc.org/element/79/gold

facts.fact: Apollo 11 first landed humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969; Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface that day.
facts.question: In what year did humans first land on the Moon?
